To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal LC-PUFA supplementation during maternal protein deficiency improves offspring brain fatty acid composition by altering the milk composition.

maternal supplementation with n -3 DHA + n -6 ARA at a low protein intake during gestation and early lactation improved brain fatty acid acc retion in rat pups, by altering the milk fat ty acid profile of the dam.

the adverse effects of protein deficiency during gestation and early lactation on long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LC-PUFAs) accretion in brain of offspring were alleviated by alterations in the milk fatty acid profile of mothers due to long-chain PUFA (DHA and ARA) supplementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of dietary protein and long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LC-PUFAs) supplementation during gestation and early lactation on the fatty acid composition of brain and milk lipids of dams and offspring.

the role of long-chain PUFA (n-3 docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and n-6 arachi-donic acid (ARA)) in fetal and neonatal development and the effects of maternal protein deficiency and supplementation with these fatty acids during pregnancy and lactation.
the effect of protein and long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LC-PUFAs) on the fatty acid composition of milk and its effect on the brain fatty acid composition of pups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LC-PUFA supplementation of the maternal diet during protein restriction improves brain LC-PUFAs of offspring by altering the milk LC-PUFA profile.

maternal supplementation with DHA and AHA during protein restriction ameliorates adverse effects of protein deficiency on the brain fatty acid profile of the offspring by increasing the DHA and AAR content in the milk and thus in the brain of the progeny.
maternal supplementation with DHA + AFA at low-protein level during gestation and postnatal life improves brain DHA accretion in pups by altering the composition of milk lipids of the dams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supplementation of n-3 LC-PUFA during pregnancy and lactation in protein-deficient mothers can improve the brain LC-PUFAs of offspring.
the maternal LC-PUFA supplementation during low-protein diet during gestation as a strategy to improve the brain LC-PUFAs status of offspring is not sufficient.
the brain of offspring of protein-restricted mothers is compromised in terms of its LC-PUFA profile, but this can be improved by maternal DHA + A RA supplementation during pregnancy and lactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal LC-PUFA supplementation at a low protein diet level can help to achieve the optimal brain PUFA status in progeny.
LC-PUFA supplementation during protein restriction can help in improving the LC-PUFA levels in brain and thus in brain development of offspring.
LC-PUFA are important for brain development during protein deficiency, and maternal LC-PUFA supplementation is an effective way to improve brain LC-PUFAs in offspring.
